The White Wall, an infernal barrier wall of imprisoned souls, gaping faces through a mottled veil

Kadagar said their God failed them
Aparal replied that they don’t know why Father Light is missing and can’t say he failed
Kadagar says that the Priests “spoke of impostors and traitors”. He forgives Aparal for his moment of weakness but threatens to brand him a traitor
Iparth Erule reports that Uhandahl was the last to drink the dragon’s blood, he tore his throat out and killed himself
Kadagar Fant has them veer into dragons and eat Kessobahn
‘We are Kessobahn’s children now, Aparal. A new father, to replace the one who abandoned us. Osserc is dead in our eyes and shall remain so. Even Father Light kneels broken, useless, and blind.’
Aparal feels such blasphemies have been said so much that the shock is gone. Pain is the only gift the Tiste Liosan understand to give to their new ‘father’
The Crippled God speaks
Even though he only has pain, misery, and suffering to offer he had worshippers that want his pity
The Crippled God is the only one that answers their prayers

Cotillion asks Edgewalker how it felt to lose everything. This is not his fear, but his weapon

Kalse dreams of ice. Ampelas dreams of ‘the rain that burns deep in shadow’

High Mage Noto Boil chewing his fish bone

I think the notion of Justice is what is worth discussing here.

Sure, by their standards, the Assail are just. They enact vengeance on behalf of the world, seeking a balance that essentially is only possible either with the world under heel or otherwise gone. The Wolves side with them because of that reason.

But Justice is cold, fundamentally opposed to compassion. How can one be human when you seek balance for every misstep? Forgiveness cannot be entertained. It doesn’t even exist. Personality hardly exists because deviances lead to free thought, differing motives, and eventually, decisions which will hurt someone. Justice may save the world, but it cannot save humanity.

I don’t think SE feels that the Assail are evil. But I do think he thinks that their stance is one fundamentally opposed to life and everything beautiful therein. In that way, there really can’t be anyone else to face at the end of the BOTF.

Nature is worth preserving and humanity is absolutely why it has declined, both in Wu and on Earth. But just eliminating humanity from the equation is a monstrosity in and of itself. Balance is required. And if we all exercised a bit more compassion, both with one another and with the natural world around us, then maybe that could be achieved.
